title: Creating dynamic sites with CMS WordPress + SEO for WordPress websites
subtitle: How to combine dynamic content management with solid SEO foundations to build sites that rank and perform.

contentBlocks.heading: Dynamic content and SEO — a powerful combo
contentBlocks.content: A static site is easy to manage when you have 5 pages. But as your content grows, you need a system. WordPress custom post types let you create structured, dynamic content — and when combined with good SEO practices, you get a site that's both scalable and discoverable.

contentBlocks.heading: Set up custom post types
contentBlocks.content: Use the Custom Post Type UI plugin or register post types manually in your theme's functions.php. Structure your content around what you publish — articles, projects, testimonials, FAQs. Each content type gets its own archive and single template, which gives you full control over how it's displayed and indexed.

contentBlocks.heading: On-page SEO essentials
contentBlocks.content: Install Rank Math or Yoast SEO. Configure your title templates, meta descriptions, and Open Graph tags. Make sure each page has a clear H1, a logical heading hierarchy, and a focus keyword that matches real search intent — not just what sounds good.

contentBlocks.heading: Site speed and Core Web Vitals
contentBlocks.content: Google's ranking algorithm weighs performance heavily. Use a caching plugin like WP Rocket, serve images in WebP format, and eliminate render-blocking scripts. Run your site through PageSpeed Insights regularly and treat it like a dashboard — not a one-time check.

contentBlocks.heading: Internal linking strategy
contentBlocks.content: Dynamic sites generate a lot of content — which means a lot of linking opportunities. Build a deliberate internal linking structure: every article should link to at least two related pieces of content. This distributes page authority and keeps users engaged longer.
